name: Alvah
overview: Alvah was a male Edomite chief, a leader among the descendants of Esau. As a chief of Edom, he held a position of authority within the Edomite tribe. The Scriptures mention him briefly, emphasizing his leadership role without additional personal details.
namesAndTitles: The primary name recorded for this individual is Alvah, with an alternate form Aliah appearing in the genealogical records. No specific meanings are provided for these names, and they are not indicated as given directly by God. The names serve primarily to identify this Edomite leader in the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Alvah as a descendant of Esau, linking him to the Edomite lineage. Beyond this connection, no further familial relationships are recorded in the biblical text concerning Alvah.
scriptureSignificance: Alvah's significance lies in his role as a chief within the Edomite nation, which descended from Esau, Jacob's brother. This leadership position reflects the organization and governance of the Edomite people as recorded in Genesis. Although briefly mentioned, Alvah's inclusion highlights the historical reality of Edomite chiefs and their place in God's providential plan for the nations.
